source_updates.title: Gradient Descent Optimization of Room Impulse Responses with Parameter-Efficient Differentiable Feedback Delay Networks
findings: sixteen-delay-line mono FDN at 48 kHz fitted on nine curated OpenAIR RIRs
no formal listening test and only informal perceptual comparison
noise-shaped baseline benefits strongly from the composite loss so architecture and loss effects are confounded
trainable delays can become near-commensurate and cause metallic ringing
fixed-delay fixed-Hadamard variant is presented as more robust at small objective cost
PEQ-10 is an RIR-specific compromise rather than a mix-EQ preset
multiplications per sample and state memory do not prove target-host callback latency
source_updates.limited_conclusion: Use only as an opt-in RIR-matching candidate with independent listening, metallicity, peak and out-of-set-room checks.

source_updates.title: Perceptual Optimisation of Loudspeaker-Based Reproduction
findings: differentiable FIR optimisation through localisation uncertainty coloration and IPD models
validation uses ideal free-field point sources one virtual source symmetric KU100 HRIRs and integer-sample delays
known panning crosstalk-cancellation and beamforming solutions are recovered under matched simulation
multi-attribute optimisation and evaluation reuse the same perceptual models
loss weights were selected by trial and error
no formal listening measured-room multi-source true-peak or headroom validation
source_updates.limited_conclusion: Research framework only; do not transfer to rock pan or width rules without independent listeners/models and measured-room multi-source validation.

knowledge_cards.claim: Lower aggregate RIR error can coexist with audible metallic ringing.
Architecture and objective contributions must be separated when a baseline improves under the new loss.
Nine curated RIRs do not establish broad room noise or truncation robustness.
Informal listening without protocol is not perceptual validation.
RIR attenuation-filter band counts are not transferable mix-EQ presets.
Operations per sample and state memory do not establish target-host callback latency.
Fixed delays and mixing are a robustness baseline when delay learning creates near-commensurate modes.
Differentiable perceptual optimisation is model optimisation rather than proof of human perceptual benefit.
Evaluation by the same perceptual model used in the loss is circular.
Free-field single-source simulation does not validate real-room multi-source spatial processing.
Trial-and-error multi-loss weights are experimental variables rather than universal constants.
Recovering known spatial solutions under matched simulation validates implementation rather than creative stereo superiority.
